bib.title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 7969-7992

question: Can a simple, generic retrieval-augmented LM decide actively when and what to retrieve during long-form generation?
hypothesis: LMs should retrieve only when they lack knowledge (low-probability tokens), and queries should reflect the intent of future generation (a drafted next sentence).
contributions: A generalized framework of active retrieval augmented generation (when and what to retrieve)
FLARE, a forward-looking method using the drafted next sentence as query when it has low-confidence tokens, applicable to existing LMs without training
Evaluation over 4 long-form knowledge-intensive tasks against single-time and multi-time retrieval baselines

method.summary: FLARE iteratively drafts the next sentence without retrieval; if any token has probability below theta, it forms a query from the draft (masking tokens below beta, or generating questions for low-confidence spans with gpt-3.5-turbo), retrieves, and regenerates the sentence. Applied to text-davinci-003 via API, no training; compared with no-retrieval, single-time, previous-window, previous-sentence and question-decomposition baselines.
method.task: long-form knowledge-intensive generation (multihop QA, commonsense QA, long-form QA, open-domain summarization)

datasets.name: 2WikiMultihopQA
datasets.split: sub-sampled at most 500; hyperparameters chosen on dev set
datasets.source: Ho et al., 2020; Wikipedia dump of Karpukhin et al. (2020)
datasets.preprocessing: retrieved docs added for the 8 exemplars

datasets.name: ASQA / ASQA-hint
datasets.preprocessing: ASQA-hint adds a hint on which aspect is ambiguous

datasets.name: WikiAsp
datasets.preprocessing: converted to open-domain by removing references; Bing retrieval with wikipedia.org, wikiwand.com, wiki2.org, wikimedia.org excluded

other.note: input length limit limits 2WikiMultihopQA to 2 retrieved docs

other.use: zero-shot question generation for explicit queries

other.corpus: Wikipedia dump of Karpukhin et al. (2020)

inference.decoding: each step generates 64 tokens, NLTK sentence tokenizer keeps first sentence; first sentence uses user input as query
inference.samples: inferred: one run per item; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.prompting: few-shot in-context learning: 8 exemplars (2Wiki), 6 (StrategyQA), 8 (ASQA, ASQA-hint), 4 (WikiAsp); retrieved docs prepended to input; only current-step docs kept
inference.retrieval: BM25 top-2 (2Wiki), top-3 (StrategyQA, ASQA), Bing top-5 (WikiAsp); previous docs discarded each step

parameters.combine single- and multi-time retrieval: no for 2Wiki, StrategyQA; yes for ASQA, ASQA-hint, WikiAsp
parameters.FLAREinstruct logit tweak: +2.0 on token '[' to encourage search; large negative on '[' for the next few tokens after a query

metrics.name: EM
metrics.definition: exact match of regex-extracted final answer (2Wiki, StrategyQA); ASQA per Stelmakh et al.

metrics.name: DR
metrics.definition: overall score combining Disambig-F1 and ROUGE

eval.protocol: Single run on at most 500 sub-sampled examples per dataset; no significance tests or seeds reported; baselines are reimplemented with the same settings, not exact reproductions

prompts.purpose: zero-shot question generation for explicit queries
prompts.text:
User input x.
Generated output so far y≤t.
Given the above passage, ask a question to which the answer is the term/entity/phrase “z”.

Search results:
[1] Document 1
[2] Document 2
...
The user input x

Now, combine the aforementioned two skills.
First, write out the reasoning steps, then draw the conclusion,
where the reasoning steps should also utilize the Search API “[Search(term)]” whenever possible.
prompts.where: Prompt D.3 (full exemplars in appendix D.3-D.10)

limits: No significant gains on Wizard of Wikipedia (short outputs, ~20 tokens) or ELI5 (grounding/evaluation issues, Krishna et al., 2021)
Interleaving retrieval and generation increases overhead and cost; LM is called once per retrieval and activations are recomputed without caching
Only text-davinci-003 tested; single run on at most 500 examples; no seeds or significance tests
Baselines are reimplementations, not exact reproductions; thetas tuned per dataset on dev
Headline Figure 4 values are in a chart only; gains on ASQA and WikiAsp are small

terms.definition: a framework that actively decides when and what to retrieve through the generation process, interleaving retrieval and generation

lineage.work: Language models (mostly) know what they know (Kadavath et al.)
lineage.note: calibration justifies confidence as a retrieval trigger

lineage.work: Precise zero-shot dense retrieval without relevance labels (HyDE; Gao et al.)
